claim: Editors can arrange a site's header and footer menus by dragging items into place and nesting them under a parent.
Each item has a type, such as a page, a link or a heading.
A parent can open as a dropdown or as a wide menu with several columns.
Every menu belongs to a site and can be set to a language, so the Welsh header can differ from the English one.
If no menu exists for a language, the menu with no language set is used.
Main, Footer and Sub-footer come with the setup command, which gives each site that has a home page its starting menus.
You can add menus under your own names.
Every item can be shown to everyone, to guests, to signed-in visitors or to a role.
Anyone who has the address can still open the page, because this hides only the link.
The Foundation theme shows all three built-in menus, and a custom menu shows only where a theme or a layout widget asks for it by name.
Menus can be published at once or on a date you choose.
Copying a site copies its menus and points the copies at the copied pages.
When you edit a menu, a preview lists the pages and sites that can show it before you save.
